related_resources.reason: Pages III–VII checked in text and selected page photographs; confirms 1904 studies, 1905 doctorate, 16 November 1913 wedding, two expeditions, 1919 Hamburg, 1924 Graz, 1930 Eismitte, 1931 search. Not a claim that the underlying private papers were examined.
Museum-linked history of 1906–08 and 1912–13 Greenland fieldwork, family, meteorology, four polar journeys, 1924 Graz and the later scientific reputation.
Birth and training, 1912 talks, 1915 book, Greenland chronology, war service, Hamburg and Graz; heading under 1914 for marriage is less precise than museum archival chronology.
1930 expedition purpose, delayed supplies and motor sleds, 21 September journey, 30 October arrival, 1 November birthday, Villumsen and unrecovered return.
Wegener geological evidence and mechanical problem, wartime 1915 work, 1929 revision, death, reception, and cautious distinction from modern tectonics.
Modern plate-tectonic evidence: ocean-floor mapping, magnetic reversals, seafloor spreading, earthquake and volcano distribution, age pattern.
Continent-fossil-climate connections, 1906 balloon, Greenland journeys, Köppen joint paleoclimate work, how Wegener handled missing forces, later scientific legacy.
Five classes of evidence for continental drift: fit, fossils, geology, tectonics and glacial deposits; 1915 text and 1930 Greenland.
1912 presentation, predecessors, geological reception, Arthur Holmes, Alexander du Toit, later plate-tectonics synthesis and 1930 expedition.
1910 conjecture, paleontological correlation, Pangaea and missing mechanism explained for nonspecialists.
History of 1912 papers and subsequent 1915/1920/1922/1929 revisions; cites Wegener’s own retrospective account of 1910/1911 observations.
Contemporaneous confirmation of two-person authorship, 1924 publication, and paleoclimate argument. Not a review of the complete book.
Documents 1926 New York debate and 1928 publication; many critics, some advocates, diverse quality of objections.
Later historiographic interpretation contests simplistic claims about the 1926 symposium; manuscript/full text not accessed.
1880, 1899–1905 education, 1906 balloon, Greenland voyages, 1913 marriage, wartime work, 1924 Graz, 1929/1930 expeditions.
Koch 1913 expedition used horses to haul supplies and sledges; recounts severe animal losses and long westward ice crossing.
Else Köppen Wegener 1892–1992, scholarly translations and editorial work, three daughters; secondary contextual support, not sole source.
Distinguishes Hess/Dietz spreading from earlier drifting continents; dates Vine–Matthews proposal and 1960s tests.
Hess and Dietz development of seafloor spreading, publication around 1961–1963, supported by Vine–Matthews and younger sea floor.
Tharp and Heezen ocean-floor mapping from 1948, 1957 Atlantic map, contribution to plate tectonics; important separate later collaboration.
Independent basic vital dates, family, marriage and institutions; German language.
Historical development of magnetic stripes and plate movement, important mid-century contributors and tests.
